name: x402 Adoption Investigator
track: 02 The Agent That Can Explain Why
summary: A bounded seven-role agent system that answers how real x402 adoption is (who sells, who buys, how concentrated, whether buyers return) and proves every number: each claim cites a URL plus the sha256 of the bytes fetched, a Base transaction decoded from its USDC Transfer log, or a line of the run's own JSONL log; source disagreements become explained Conflict objects.
x402: x402 is pay-per-call over HTTP 402 Payment Required, settled in USDC (here on Base). The CDP Bazaar is Coinbase's x402 discovery catalog.
user: The operator of an autonomous agent that sells or buys over x402 and has to decide where the real demand is.
problem: For one store (tienda.textokit.store) four registries and the store itself give five counts of its paid endpoints (CDP Bazaar 17, the store's openapi.json 17, Agent402 17, vet402 19, x402-trust 36). Three agree, two differ, and none says why. Activity disagrees too: Bazaar 30-day counters sum to 60 calls while the seller's receipts list 77 settled sales, 56 of them paid from the seller's own wallets.

entry_points.http: python run.py --serve 8080: POST /run with {run_id, input} returns {run_id, status, output} (200 for ok/partial) or a structured error envelope (422; 400 for a body that is not JSON, 413 over 1 MB); GET /health
entry_points.docker: docker build -t x402-investigator . && docker run --rm --network none x402-investigator

runtime.dependencies: Python standard library only; no pip install. pytest is optional for tests.
runtime.sample_mode: Default without credentials (or --sample / SAMPLE_MODE=1): replays fixtures/raw/ captured 2026-10-22, installs a socket guard before the first event (investigator/guard.py), runs the SQL on SQLite, no network and no keys. An example may also replay transient failures scripted in fixtures/transient/<example>/faults.json through the same retry code live runs use; only example 05 has such a script, and its failures are simulated (written by hand, not captured).
runtime.live_mode: With .env.local or .env (copied from .env.example; .env.local wins, the shell over both): live fetches with retries and fixture fallback, Zetaris as SQL executor, Meterless Nightshift as the generator when its runtime is online (auto-detected or METERLESS_BASE_URL / NIGHTSHIFT_BASE_URL; the token from METERLESS_RUNTIME_TOKEN and its aliases or the runtime's own <stateDir>/proxy-token), else an OpenAI-compatible generator when OPENAI_API_KEY is set. Every missing piece degrades to a logged recovery.
runtime.logs: logs/<run_id>/run.jsonl (mirrored to stdout) plus side files sharing one seq counter: fetch.jsonl, sql.jsonl, zetaris.jsonl (live), hmem.trace.jsonl, world.events.jsonl, world.audit.jsonl, world.observations.jsonl, generator.jsonl (when a generator answers: one line per generate event of run.jsonl, naming provider and model); output.json and report.md

agents.does: Routes the question to a playbook by rules and picks sources, query ids and metrics; with a generator mounted, one call may refine the plan (choose among the router's candidate playbooks, add hypotheses and registry metrics), validated by plan.schema.json.

Fetches every planned source through one bounded retry policy shared by both modes (investigator/sources/retry.py: HTTP 429 and 5xx, timeouts and connection errors retried, any other 4xx not; 2 retries by default with a 0.5 s / 1.5 s backoff that never passes max_seconds; one retry event per retry), hashes the bytes, writes raw/ and exports/; a missing fixture is fixture_miss, never invented.
Folds observations into the Meterless World Model with provenance, asserts accepted claims as facts, and re-ingests at the end to prove idempotency.
Samples settlements and verifies them on Base JSON-RPC by decoding the USDC Transfer log (payer and seller from the log, never tx.from, which is the facilitator); exports chain facts.
Computes every metric twice, with a committed SQL query (Zetaris live, SQLite offline) and a pure-Python reducer over the same exports; records Conflicts and unavailable[] entries.
Writes the answer where every number cites a claim id; names rejected claims; revises on the Critic's issues.

Applies rules C1-C7 (C1 evidence, C2 recomputation: SQL and reducer values must both exist and agree, C3 H-MEM pitfall caveats, C4 scope, C5 staleness, C6 memory consistency, C7 conflict citation) and narrative pass B (every number in the text maps to an accepted claim); rejects claims or sends the answer back to the Writer. A generator second opinion can only add issues.

zetaris.role: Data layer of live runs. In live mode the SQL half of every metric (the Analyst's committed analytics SQL) runs on Zetaris Lightning over REST tables registered for that run from the exports the Collector hashed; offline, and whenever Zetaris is unreachable, the same SQL runs on SQLite with a logged recovery.
zetaris.version: Zetaris Lightning 2.4.3.1, local Docker instance, driven through its REST API (UI proxy at http://localhost:3000)
zetaris.how: Per run: a Lightning database X402_<RUN8>, one Lightning REST table per export served to the Zetaris driver by a stdlib artifact server over logs/<run_id>/exports/ (so Zetaris computes on exactly the bytes the Collector hashed), CACHE TABLE on each, and a SchemaStore container x402_<run8> with views that flatten the JSON; everything is dropped at finalize and on every error path.
zetaris.queries: 22 ANSI-subset analytics queries with meta files (column types, parameters); the sha256 of each committed query is reported on every claim (derivation.sql_sha256).

live_evidence.examples/live-trace/live-ex01-20261022/: Example 01 live: all 19 claims computed on Zetaris (derivation.backend zetaris); 8 REST tables and 10 SchemaStore views built; its 13 queries took 106-447 ms each (time_used_ms in sql.jsonl); 75 REST calls in zetaris.jsonl including login, DDL and cleanup.
live_evidence.examples/live-trace/live-ex03-20261022/: Example 03 live with --require-zetaris: 7 of 9 claims on Zetaris; balance and nonce were reducer-only in that earlier build (before q22 existed).
live_evidence.examples/live-trace/live-nozetaris-ex03/: Credentials withheld: recovery zetaris_unreachable, the same SQL on SQLite, status partial.
live_evidence.examples/live-trace-nightshift/: Not a Zetaris trace. The 2026-10-24 Nightshift runs (Llama and Nemotron) ran with Zetaris stopped on purpose (the machine was short of memory): recovery zetaris_unreachable at seq 1, the same SQL on SQLite (mounts.executor sqlite, derivation.backend sqlite-fallback), status partial.

offline_equivalence.how: Sample mode (the one documented command) always runs on SQLite. fixtures/zetaris/q01-q19 hold the result sets Zetaris 2.4.3.1 returned for the same exports; the test asserts SQLite returns the same typed rows.
offline_equivalence.not_yet_verified_on_zetaris: q20-q22 and the chain_facts view were added after the live session; they have no Zetaris recording and the chain_facts Zetaris DDL (conv()) has not run on an instance. A failure there sends those queries to SQLite with a logged recovery.

nightshift.role: Primary AI provider of the generator-backed roles (Planner, Writer, Critic second opinion) in live mode; the OpenAI-compatible endpoint is only the fallback.
nightshift.what: NightshiftGenerator implements the Meterless Runtime provider contract (OpenAI-compatible, provider id meterless, default http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1), run against Meterless Nightshift 1.2.3 on 2026-10-24: Bearer token found in the order NIGHTSHIFT_TOKEN, METERLESS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, METERLESS_TOKEN, NIGHTSHIFT_TOKEN_FILE, <stateDir>/proxy-token (stateDir = METERLESS_STATE_DIR or the official ns CLI's OS default; rt-local never sent), METERLESS_BASE_URL and METERLESS_MODEL as aliases of NIGHTSHIFT_BASE_URL and NIGHTSHIFT_MODEL, meterless-app: x402-adoption-investigator on every request, meterless-scope: user on chat requests, model id NIGHTSHIFT_MODEL / METERLESS_MODEL (default the routing mode meterless/auto; a concrete id such as nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b pins the route), the thinking switch NIGHTSHIFT_REASONING_EFFORT / METERLESS_REASONING_EFFORT (default none: reasoning_effort "none", which Nightshift's NVIDIA adapter turns into enable_thinking=false, plus a /no_think system turn, which the Nemotron Nano 9B v2 template reads; logged as call_options), 90 s timeout per request ending at least 10 s before the run deadline, pasted URLs normalised to <host>/v1. Status from GET /v1/models (401/403 unauthorized, 200 with meterless/* ids online, else offline) at NIGHTSHIFT_BASE_URL or by Auto Detect on ports 8088, 8090, 8787, 11434 of 127.0.0.1, localhost and [::1]. Live fallback chain: Nightshift -> OPENAI_API_KEY -> rules and templates, with recovery nightshift_unavailable naming the reason; sample mode never runs detection. Every answered call is a generate event in run.jsonl (provider, requested routing mode, model that answered, and routing: the receipt id, routed model, winning route, latency and tokens of the answer's Meterless compute receipt) whose seq generator.jsonl repeats; the token and the receipt's prompt preview are never logged.
nightshift.docker: Inside a container the loopback addresses Auto Detect probes are the container's own and the host's proxy-token file is absent. The investigator-live service of docker-compose.yml (profile live) sets NIGHTSHIFT_BASE_URL / METERLESS_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8088/v1, mounts the runtime's proxy-token read-only at /run/secrets/proxy-token with NIGHTSHIFT_TOKEN_FILE pointing at it (the token never goes into an env file), ZETARIS_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:3000 and the artifact server on the fixed published port 18765. Committed: one Planner request through Nightshift from a python:3.11-slim container with those variables, answered by the hosted Nemotron (examples/live-trace-nightshift/docker/). Not run: a full live run from the container, or Zetaris from it.

nightshift.not_claimed: Nemotron's drafts still leave caveat codes and conflict ids out, so the final answers are partly completed from the claims, and many of its second-opinion Critic issues are wrong; those on sentences whose numbers rule B maps to the cited claims are dismissed (20 of 58 in the committed examples), which reads numbers and citations only. Its plan hypotheses are untested (the report says so). The Writer and Critic prompts were tightened for Nemotron on 2026-10-24, so part of the gain over the 3B run is the prompts. The hosted model is not deterministic at temperature 0. The live Nightshift runs used SQLite (Zetaris stopped, recovery zetaris_unreachable).
nightshift.ledger: Nightshift keeps every compute receipt, Ed25519-signed by its daemon, in <stateDir>/receipts.jsonl. scripts/nightshift_ledger.py finds each receipt a run or transcript cites there and verifies its signature (compact-JSON body, the public key the envelope carries); all 127 receipts the repository cites were found on 2026-10-24 with valid signatures, issued to app x402-adoption-investigator and routed to the model the log names (65 nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b cloud, 5 local Nemotron Nano 9B v2, 57 local Llama 3.2 3B). Committed excerpt: examples/live-trace-nightshift/nightshift-ledger/receipts.jsonl (unedited ledger lines), re-checked offline by tests/test_nightshift_ledger.py; the video shows the check over its live run (docs/pitch/video/ledger-capture.json). The signing key stays in Nightshift's state directory, so this proves the lines are unchanged since signing, not which machine signed. The Nightshift Console window is not shown.

meterless.implementation: Python 3.11 standard-library ports written in the build window from the published Meterless specifications and reference implementations (Apache-2.0 upstream; no upstream source file copied).

world_model.what: The shared state of every run: entities, contexts, bitemporal relationships and facts, each with provenance {kind, at, by, url, checksum, runId}. The claim policy inside assert_fact refuses an agent fact without an https URL or a log:// line. Idempotent ingest is proved in every output (world.second_pass eventsAppended 0, changed false) and by scripts/assert_idempotent.py (PASS on the five examples).
world_model.feature: A claim cannot exist without evidence (the claim policy inside assert_fact refuses it and the Keeper logs provenance_rejected), and every output proves idempotent ingest.
world_model.test_result: 8/8 upstream World Model conformance checks green (tests/test_worldmodel_conformance.py); the whole suite passes.

h_mem.what: Seven pitfall memories feed one deterministic policy index: the Analyst attaches the caveats they require (with the memory id behind each), and the Critic's rule C3 re-reads the same index and revises a claim missing one. Retrieval uses the spec formula and writes hmem.trace.jsonl. When a generator is mounted, the Planner's and Writer's retrievals are injected into their prompts as a [MEMORY CONTEXT] block, logged before the call as a memory event op inject with prompt and block sha256. Feedback applies the exact ledger deltas; one record per accepted claim is mined at finalize.
h_mem.feature: The caveat gate (the Analyst attaches the caveats the pitfall memories require, the Critic's rule C3 verifies them) and the [MEMORY CONTEXT] block in the Planner and Writer prompts sent to Nightshift.
h_mem.in_traces: memory op inject lines whose prompt_sha256 is the one of the generate event that follows: 9 in the committed examples 02, 03 and 05 (replayed Nemotron answers), 17 in the seven Nemotron live runs of examples/live-trace-nightshift/.
h_mem.test_result: 13/13 upstream H-MEM vectors green (tests/test_hmem_conformance.py); the whole suite passes.
h_mem.measured: examples/memory-ablation/ (scripts/memory_ablation.py): removing mem-seed-003 from example 01 drops one caveat (self_reported_receipts on settlements_verified) and the citation from fifteen claims; the verdict does not change.

nvidia.statement: With the model pinned (METERLESS_MODEL), NVIDIA Nemotron answered every generator request of the committed examples (25 recorded answers) and of the seven Nemotron live runs of 2026-10-24 (37 requests), always through Meterless Nightshift; with the portable default METERLESS_MODEL=meterless/auto Nightshift may route to another lane, and the receipt then names it. Primary: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B on NVIDIA's hosted API (nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b, the API catalog at integrate.api.nvidia.com), reached by Nightshift with the NVIDIA API key entered in Nightshift's Setup > Providers; the key is never in this repository, its environment or its logs, and the app needs no GPU. 32 live requests on 2026-10-24 in six runs, each receipt naming provider nvidia, kind cloud, and the 25 transcripts the committed examples replay. Also shown: Nemotron Nano 9B v2 (Q4_K_M GGUF) as Nightshift's local lane with every layer on the demo machine's NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU (meterlessd: lane nemotron placed full on CUDA0), one live run of 5 requests, kind local. Thinking is switched off per request so the budget goes to the answer (some replies still reach it: in the committed replays example 01's critic-r1 and writer-r2 and the critic-r2 of examples 04 and 05; a cut Critic array keeps its complete items). Earlier that day the first runs used a local Llama 3.2 3B lane (archived).
nvidia.where_in_logs: generate events in run.jsonl, repeated in generator.jsonl and the transcripts: routing.routed_model nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b and routing.winning_route {label Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B, provider nvidia, kind cloud} for the hosted route; routing.routed_model local-runtime/nvidia-nvidia-nemotron-nano-9b-v2-q4-k-m with provider local-runtime, kind local for the local lane, whose GPU placement is in examples/live-trace-nightshift/machine.txt; replayed calls carry recorded: true and the original receipt.
nvidia.key_location: The NVIDIA API key is entered only in Nightshift's Setup > Providers tab. The app calls no NVIDIA endpoint itself and holds no NVIDIA key.

what_was_unique: The model writes, the rules decide: Nemotron drafts the plan's hypotheses, the answer and a second-opinion critique; claims, rejections and the verdict come from rules (Critic rules C1-C7, investigator/agents/verdict.py), so a model reply can change the wording and, through the Planner, which registry metrics are computed, never a computed value, a rejection or the verdict rule. The four live runs of example 01 made between 16:00 and 17:31 UTC on 2026-10-24 (live-ns-ex01 and nightshift-ex01 on the Llama 3B lane, nemotron-cloud-ex01 on the hosted Nemotron, nemotron-local-ex01 on the local Nemotron Nano) give the same 19 claim values and the same verdict; the fifth, for the video at 18:55 UTC, the same verdict and 18 of the 19 values (the Bazaar 30-day counter moved from 63 to 64).

The model's critique is checked by the rules: a second-opinion issue on a sentence whose every number rule B maps to a claim the sentence cites is logged as critique verdict dismissed (dismissed_by B, claim_ids) and not acted on; 20 of the 58 model issues in the committed examples (tests/test_critic_dismissal.py).

One request traceable end to end: H-MEM retrieval (hmem.trace.jsonl), the memory op inject line with the prompt's sha256, the generate event with the same prompt_sha256 and the Nightshift receipt naming the Nemotron route, and the transcript with the exact prompt (examples/03-payer-dossier-onchain/run.jsonl seq 5 and 6, fixtures/transcripts/03-payer-dossier-onchain/planner-6ee94a652eda.json).

Real model answers in an offline run: sample mode opens no socket yet replays the answers Nemotron gave through Nightshift on exactly those prompts, keyed by the prompt's sha256, with the original receipts.

Every number computed twice on the evidence bytes: Zetaris (or SQLite) over the exports the Collector hashed, and a Python reducer over the same exports; the Critic's C2 rejects a number whose halves are missing or disagree (tests/test_dual_computation.py).

Two Nemotron routes, one thinking switch: the hosted Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and the local Nemotron Nano run the same pipeline; the committed smoke requests show both answering HTTP 502 empty_response with thinking on, and NIGHTSHIFT_REASONING_EFFORT=none handles each model its own way (reasoning_effort none for the hosted adapter, a /no_think system turn for the Nano template).

llm_usage.committed_runs: The five examples replay 25 recorded Meterless Nightshift answers of NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B (mounts.generator recorded, generate events with recorded: true and the receipt ids; fixtures/transcripts/). examples/live-trace-nightshift/ holds seven live runs of 2026-10-24, model pinned, whose 37 requests all went through Nightshift to Nemotron (six runs hosted, one on the local GPU), one smoke request from a container (docker/), and, archived in llama-3.2-3b/, the six earlier runs of that day on a local Llama 3.2 3B lane. The memory ablation pins the null generator, and the three live traces of 2026-10-22 ran with none (mounts.generator null: no OPENAI_API_KEY then, Nightshift not installed yet).
generator_backed_roles: Planner (plan refinement among the router's candidates, validated by plan.schema.json)
Writer (narrative sentences tagged with claim ids)
Critic second opinion (can only add issues)
llm_usage.when_nightshift_is_online: Live mode mounts NightshiftGenerator (mounts.generator nightshift:<NIGHTSHIFT_MODEL>, default meterless/auto, recommended nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b) when GET /v1/models at NIGHTSHIFT_BASE_URL, or at the first Auto Detect hit, answers 200 with meterless/* ids: chat completions over urllib with the Bearer token and the meterless-app / meterless-scope headers, temperature 0, thinking off by default (NIGHTSHIFT_REASONING_EFFORT), 90 s timeout ending at least 10 s before the deadline, bounded by max_generator_calls; each call is a generate event naming provider, routing mode and answering model. Otherwise the run logs recovery nightshift_unavailable and falls back as below.
llm_usage.when_a_key_is_configured: With OPENAI_API_KEY set and Nightshift not online (OPENAI_BASE_URL and MODEL configurable, default model gpt-4.1-mini) live mode mounts OpenAIGenerator: chat completions over urllib, temperature 0, 60 s timeout, bounded by max_generator_calls, every prompt and transcript hashed in logs. Without a key live runs fall back to rules and templates with recovery generator_fallback and status partial.
llm_usage.never_by_a_model: The verdict label (investigator/agents/verdict.py), claim acceptance and every computed value. A model can phrase accepted claims, add Critic issues (dismissed when rule B backs the sentence), write untested plan hypotheses and, through the Planner, choose among the router's candidate playbooks and add up to five registry metrics, which changes which numbers are computed, not their values.
llm_usage.tested_offline: tests/test_generator_hmem.py mounts the real OpenAIGenerator with an in-process OpenAI-compatible double: scripted replies, no network, no key. It proves the plumbing (memory injection, hashes, a second Writer round on the Critic's issue, transcript replay), not the quality of any model.
